messages.subject: [rkward-users] Donate to Rkward
messages.body_plain:
Hi, sorry for bringing up an old thread, but I see that PayPal is still 
the only way to donate. Have developers considered using Software in the 
Public Interest, Inc. (www.spi-inc.org) as a donation portal? It also 
acts as fiscal sponsor. I'm unsure whether this is right for a project 
like Rkward, but I see some individual applications being listed as 
beneficiaries. I just found out about this project and thought it could 
be useful.

--Alex

On 03/31/2011 07:08 AM, Thomas Friedrichsmeier wrote:
> Hi,
>
> On Thursday 31 March 2011, Alex Ruiz Euler wrote:
>> Is there a way to donate that is not via PayPal? I would love to give
>> something to the extent that my overstretched grad student paycheck
>> allows, but I don't want to do it with PP.
> I can totally understand your reluctance to use PayPal. However, at the
> moment, it's the only option that our host (sourceforge) supports. Perhaps it
> will make sense to provide one more option in the future, but in fact, I
> wouldn't know which one to pick. Any recommendations on a payment service that
> is
> - international / cross currency
> - mostly fair
> - widely in use?
>
>> Also, some friends and I have had some hypothesis about how you
>> pronounce Rkward. Most of them are pretty weird. For example, one claims
>> that it is supposed to go with an Australian accent playing on the word
>> awkward because most of us users are probably, well, awkward.
> Well, as far as the pronounciation goes, that is the "correct" interpretation.
> But you shouldn't go looking for any deeper meaning. When I first registered
> the project, way back then, I simply did not spend a whole lot of time
> thinking about a good name. I stuck to the constraint that the name should
> contain the letters R and K. "Ark" and "Kross" were taken, already, and I
> didn't think much beyond that. So that's how RKWard ended up with its awkward
> name. I guess it's not the name that I would pick today, but I still sort of
> like the self-referential aspect of it...
>
>> Another
>> has the incredible hypothesis that you actually pronounce it Rkward, but
>> that is really awkward too. So... how to pronounce it?
> Actually, that pronounciation is totally fine with me, as well. Whatever you
> feel is least (or most) awkward.
>
> Regards
> Thomas
>

donating to RKWard. Admittedly, you'd need true eagle eyes to see this: So 
far, there's just a tiny button below the left-hand navigation menu on our

FAQ seems to say, only the receiving side needs a paypal account, but I did 
not find any real info on their payment options, yet).

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: [rkward-users] [rkward-announce] SVN repository URL has changed
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

The URL of the RKWard SVN repository has changed. Those tracking SVN, please 
refer to http://sourceforge.net/p/rkward/code/ for the new URL(s).

In general, the safest thing to do is to check out a fresh working copy. 
However, esp. if you have any local changes in your working copy, you can also 
"switch" your working copy to the new location. To do so, run
   svn info
Note the given URL. Copy the new url from the above web page, then run
   svn switch --relocate old_url new_url

In case of problems, just ask.

Note that it may take us a while to update links to the SVN repository, 
everywhere applicable. However, if you happen to come across any references to 
the previous location 
(http(s)://rkward.svn.sourceforge.net/svnroot/rkward/trunk/) after the end of 
the week, please let us know.

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: [rkward-users] svn update: important for MacPorts users
messages.subject_clean: [rkward-users] svn update: important for MacPorts users
messages.body_plain:
hi,

for those of you who are *building* RKWard with MacPorts, please make sure you 
are using an up-to-date portfile. all others: please ignore this e-mail.

the old portfiles will fail soon, as they refer to the now outdated svn 
repository. the latest development portfile can be found here:
 http://svn.code.sf.net/p/rkward/code/trunk/rkward/macports/kde/rkward/Portfile

if you want to build the stable 0.6.0 release, use this one instead:
 http://svn.code.sf.net/p/rkward/code/trunk/rkward/macports/kde/rkward/Portfile.release
and remove the ".release" suffix.

the wiki has been updated accordingly:
http://sourceforge.net/apps/mediawiki/rkward/index.php?title=RKWard_on_Mac#Installing_from_source_using_MacPorts

On Wednesday 30 January 2013, NoSkill ButStyle wrote:
> I downloaded the latest update today, and now the R syntax highlightning
> looks different. For example, functions are not bold anymore, as well as
> Text after ##.
> 
> Is there a way to switch back to the old look? I tried to edit Settings ->
> Configure Editor -> Fonts & Colors -> Highlightning Text Styles ->
> Scripts/R-Script, but there still the "old" styles are shown which do not
> correspond to what the editor highlights. Furthermore, there I cannot
> change any options, e.g. I cannot uncheck or check boxes.

nothing has changed in RKWard 0.6.0 with respect to highlighting. The problem 
must be related to a change in some other package, e.g. in kdelibs. Could you 
provide details on your distribution (some flavor of Ubuntu, IIRC?) and 
installed version of KDE?

The settings page you are looking at is the correct one, indeed. Here, these 
settings correspond to what I'm seeing, and I can change options, successfully 
(some of the check boxes seem to need more than one click to react, though).

Do you get any highlighting at all? Could it be you switched to a different 
highlighting mode, somehow (Edit->Tools Move->Highlighting, for the active 
script, or Settings->Configure Editor->Open/Save->Modes & Filetypes for the 
default highlighting mode)?

Regards
Thomas

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On Wednesday 30 January 2013, NoSkill ButStyle wrote:
> I checked the highlightening modes as you described, but they seem to be
> correct.
> 
> I get some kind of highlightning, which looks like this:
> http://www.abload.de/img/ulhoswj.png

this looks like R highlighting, indeed. AFAICS, it's just the bold font 
weights that are missing. Perhaps this is the core of the problem, really. 
Possibly this is related to the font / font system in use?

Some things to try:
- Try adjusting some other attribute (e.g. color). Does this show an effect 
(function names use the "Keyword" attribute, ## comments use "Headline").
- Open an R script in kwrite or kate. Does this show the correct styles? Are 
the styles adjustable, here?
- Try selecting a different font at Settings->Configure Editor->Fonts & 
Colors>Font. Does this help?

Regards
Thomas
